Verbatim relay does NOT use httplib Response::set_content: this vcpkg build has brotli support, so set_content would gzip/brotli the body whenever the caller sent Accept-Encoding, adding Content-Encoding/Vary the upstream never sent. Buffered relays use a fixed-length content provider instead, which httplib does not re-encode. Tests would have passed either way (the client decompresses transparently) — this is about being verbatim ON THE WIRE.

SSE needs a worker thread: httplib invokes the server-side chunked content provider AFTER the handler returns, and the client's send() blocks, so both cannot be driven from one thread. Lifetime is owned by a detail::UpstreamCall captured in the provider lambda; its destructor cancels + client->stop() + joins, so a downstream disconnect can neither leak nor wedge a thread.
TCP_NODELAY enabled on both legs (httplib defaults it off) — right for token-by-token SSE and removes Nagle as a flake source.

G5 fail-soft verified in the implementation, not just the tests: json::parse uses allow_exceptions=false, dump() is wrapped so an un-round-trippable body forwards ORIGINAL bytes, and the only minted status is the 502 for an unreachable upstream.

KNOWN MINOR, raised at the Phase 11 gate: AdmissionController::policies_ is erased only in grantNext (when a model's queue empties or its last entry is granted), so a model whose CONTENDED queue drains entirely by queueTimeout rather than by grant leaves one AffinityPolicy behind. Bounded by distinct model names ever contended; G13 pins one model, so it is inert today. The fix would need an O(n) scan in the timeout path, which is why it was not taken now.

The policy is PURE (no clock, no randomness, no global state) and is consulted from grantNext under the mutex admission already holds — no second queue, no second lock. 'Queued at selection time' is derived from the monotonic arrival ordinal (a per-burst ceiling), so the policy needs neither a clock nor an extra parameter.
